column3: Now about that time Herod the king laid hands on some from the assembly to mistreat them.
He killed James the brother of John with the sword.
And seeing that it was pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter also. Those were the days of Unleavened Bread.
After seizing him, he put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending after the Passover to bring him out to the people.
So Peter was being kept in prison, but earnest prayer was being made by the assembly to God for him.
Now when Herod was about to bring him out, that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping watch over the prison.
And look, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. Striking Peter on the side, he woke him, saying, “Get up quickly!” And the chains fell from his hands.
The angel said to him, “Gird yourself and tie on your sandals.” And he did so. Then he said to him, “Put your cloak around you and follow me.”
And going out, he followed him, and he did not know that what was happening through the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision.

After passing the first guard and the second, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened to them by itself. And after going out, they went along one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.
Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I truly know that the Lord sent out his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the Jewish people.”
And realizing this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, who was surnamed Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.
When he knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
And recognizing Peter’s voice, because of her joy she did not open the gate, but ran in and reported that Peter was standing before the gate.
They said to her, “You are out of your mind!” But she kept insisting that it was so. They were saying, “It is his angel.”
But Peter continued knocking, and when they opened, they saw him and were astonished.

But motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he described to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, “Report these things to James and the brothers.” Then he went out and traveled to another place.
Now when day came, there was no small disturbance among the soldiers as to what had happened to Peter.
And after Herod searched for him and did not find him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away to execution. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Now he was angrily disposed toward the Tyrians and Sidonians. But they came to him with one accord, and after persuading Blastus, who was over the king’s bedchamber, they asked for peace, because their country was fed by the king’s country.
On an appointed day Herod put on royal clothing, sat on the judgment seat, and began addressing them publicly.
The people began shouting, “The voice of a god and not of a man!”
Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he did not give the glory to God, and being eaten by worms, he died.
But the word of God kept growing and multiplying.
And Barnabas and Saul returned after completing their service, taking along John, the one surnamed Mark.
